deck.title: Safety, Health, Environmental Management and Audit Systems Concept Cards

concepts.canonicalLabel: Occupational Health and Safety Management System

cards.backDefinition: The organized set of interrelated policies, processes, responsibilities, controls, and activities an organization uses to achieve defined objectives and manage performance in a systematic way.
cards.whyItMatters: A management system connects leadership, planning, operations, checking, and improvement instead of treating safety, health, or environmental controls as isolated activities.
cards.keyPoint: Think of a management system as the coordinated way an organization manages related parts of its business to achieve objectives.

sourceRefs.locator: Management system standards > What is a management system?

cards.backDefinition: A family of ISO environmental management standards covering environmental management systems and supporting topics such as implementation, auditing, communication, labelling, life-cycle approaches, and environmental performance.
cards.whyItMatters: Recognizing the family prevents the common mistake of treating ISO 14000 as one certifiable standard; ISO 14001 is the central requirements standard within the broader family.
cards.keyPoint: ISO 14000 is a family; ISO 14001 is the certifiable environmental management system requirements standard.

sourceRefs.locator: ISO 14000 family — Environmental management > family scope and ISO 14001 role

cards.backDefinition: The current ISO requirements standard for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an environmental management system so an organization can systematically manage its environmental responsibilities.
cards.whyItMatters: It provides the main certifiable environmental management system framework within the ISO 14000 family and is relevant wherever environmental aspects, compliance obligations, objectives, controls, and improvement must be managed systematically.
cards.keyPoint: As of September 2026, ISO 14001:2026 is the current published edition.

sourceRefs.locator: ISO 14001:2026 — Environmental management systems — Requirements with guidance for use
ISO 14000 family > ISO 14001 is the certifiable EMS standard

cards.backDefinition: The part of an organization's management system used to manage environmental aspects, fulfil applicable environmental obligations, achieve environmental objectives, and improve environmental performance.
cards.whyItMatters: An EMS turns environmental commitments into an organized operating system of responsibilities, planning, controls, monitoring, evaluation, and continual improvement.
cards.keyPoint: An EMS is the management framework; ISO 14001 provides requirements for that framework.

cards.backDefinition: The current published ISO requirements standard for an occupational health and safety management system, providing a framework to manage OH&S risks, improve performance, prevent work-related injury and ill health, and support continual improvement.
cards.whyItMatters: It gives organizations an internationally recognized systems framework that integrates leadership, worker participation, hazard and risk management, operational controls, performance evaluation, and improvement.
cards.keyPoint: As of September 2026, ISO 45001:2018 remains the current published edition; a replacement edition is still under development.

sourceRefs.locator: ISO 45001:2018 — Occupational health and safety management systems

cards.frontLabel: Occupational Health and Safety Management System
cards.backDefinition: The management-system framework an organization uses to establish OH&S policy and objectives, manage hazards and risks, involve workers, implement controls, evaluate performance, and continually improve occupational health and safety outcomes.
cards.whyItMatters: An OHSMS organizes safety and health responsibilities into a repeatable business system rather than relying only on individual rules, inspections, or reactive incident responses.
cards.keyPoint: ISO 45001 and ANSI/ASSP Z10 are two recognized frameworks for occupational health and safety management systems.

cards.backDefinition: The current ISO guidance standard for auditing management systems, covering audit principles, management of audit programmes, conducting management-system audits, and the competence and evaluation of auditors.
cards.whyItMatters: It provides a common auditing framework that can be applied across management systems such as environmental, quality, and occupational health and safety systems.
cards.keyPoint: ISO 19011:2026 guides auditing; it does not itself establish a certifiable management system.

sourceRefs.locator: ISO 19011:2026 — Guidelines for auditing management systems

cards.backDefinition: A systematic audit used to evaluate a management system against defined audit criteria and determine whether arrangements are implemented and effective enough to support the organization's objectives and conformity needs.
cards.whyItMatters: Management-system audits provide structured evidence about how the system is functioning, where requirements are not met, and where improvement is needed.
cards.keyPoint: The audit evaluates the system against defined criteria; it is more than a general workplace inspection.

cards.backDefinition: The organized arrangements for one or more audits over a planned period, including objectives, scope priorities, resources, responsibilities, scheduling, monitoring, review, and improvement of the auditing activity.
cards.whyItMatters: Managing audits as a programme helps organizations prioritize risk, coordinate resources, maintain consistency, and ensure that important parts of the management system receive appropriate audit attention.
cards.keyPoint: An audit programme manages the overall set of audits; an individual audit is one activity within that programme.

cards.backDefinition: A U.S. national consensus standard that provides a systems-based framework for establishing and improving an occupational health and safety management system that organizations can tailor to their risks and operating context.
cards.whyItMatters: Z10 gives organizations a recognized U.S. consensus framework for integrating occupational safety and health into business systems and continually improving OSH performance.
cards.keyPoint: ANSI/ASSP Z10 is an occupational health and safety management-system standard, not an environmental management standard.

sourceRefs.locator: ANSI/ASSP Z10 OSH Management Standard > What is the Z10.0 standard?

cards.backDefinition: A recurring management-system improvement model in which an organization plans objectives and processes, implements them, checks performance and results, and acts on findings to correct or improve the system.
cards.whyItMatters: PDCA provides a simple structure for linking planning, implementation, performance evaluation, and continual improvement across management-system activities.
cards.keyPoint: Plan sets direction, Do implements, Check evaluates, and Act improves.

cards.backDefinition: Independent third-party confirmation by a certification body that an organization's management system conforms to the requirements of a certifiable management-system standard; certification is optional unless separately required by a customer, contract, or other obligation.
cards.whyItMatters: Recognizing the distinction prevents the misconception that implementing an ISO management system automatically means the organization is certified or that ISO itself performs certification.
cards.keyPoint: An organization can implement a management-system standard without certification; ISO does not certify organizations.
